fact: Africa Frontline First and Living Goods state that community health worker data are not integrated into the national health information system (DHIS2/ENDOS), most community health workers still use paper tools, and a roadmap prioritising that integration was co-created by the Ministry of Health with Africa CDC, Living Goods and UNICEF at a workshop on 8-12 September 2025, with finalisation, validation and resourcing still to come.

A Johns Hopkins and Université Joseph Ki-Zerbo evaluation in Toma district found limited integration between the REC-Maternity tablet tool and DHIS2, with parallel paper and electronic flows (REC-Maternity to DHIS2 record ratios of 1.56 for postnatal care and 3.05 for family planning in 2021) and facilities still summarising paper forms for district staff to enter into DHIS2; dated to the study's 2021 endline because the paper gives no later date.
